title: Dummy PR, to check Heroku
body:
We're getting lots of builds failing on Heroku.  They were intermittent, but are now happening more often.

This is a branch from a commit from a few weeks ago (16th September), to see if the build problem is because of something we have introduced.

comments_data.body: Ok. 16th Sept builds.  Getting Heroku to deploy again, just to test.
Ok, this built several times.  That's interesting, but not useful in fixing current build.  That's being addressed in #1936

issues.title: Heroku build issue
issues.body:
[this is to track the issue with the Heroku build]

## 09:00

We did have an intermittent Heroku build issue, where PRs occasionally failed to build. I was able to overcome it by closing/re-opening the PR.

But, it's not easy to do that in the `serge-review` or `serge-sql` persistent deployments.  

The current state is that version of Serge on `serge-sql` is dated 12th October.  _Maybe_ that's the date that a problem arose.

I've just made a PR with a checkout from 16th September, and it worked ok.  That does suggest its something changing in Serge that has caused the issue.

The Heroku build always failed on exactly the same line: ` @serge/client: Creating an optimized production build...` _Maybe_ that suggests it's a build issue in the `client` package, but that's just a guess. Full listing further below.  

I've had a look at changes from 6 days ago.  Amongst lost of updates, we changed this in `client\package.json`:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/196374344-94482e3b-2541-433a-9eb9-b5be6b180105.png)

Here is what Heroku says about memory:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/196376822-07334f62-e4bf-484d-80a0-049fbabf227d.png)

I'll make a PR and try to revert that.

## 10:00

I reduced the memory to 2Gb, and did local build. The compile repeatedly failed.  I tried increasing the memory, but the build repeatedly failed with `You gave us a visitor for the node type TSInstantiationExpression but it’s not a valid type`.  I increased memory to 8Gb, and it was still failing. So, I googled the above issue, and was told to "remove node_packages; remove yarn.lock; run yarn".  I did that, and the build worked (even with 2Gb).  I pushed that branch, but it failed at Heroku (out of memory).  So, I'm going to experiment with increasing memory on Heroku.
